title: spec review: S2b memory_scorecard and memory_eval: retrieval precision, downstream use, utility per token, and the P34 memory eval cases (P5, P34 memory)
spec:
Create orchestrator/memory_scorecard.py: read decision_log rows of kind retrieval (the kind T-1151 writes for memory retrievals; there is no memory_retrieval kind) and the bus outcome of their subject tasks. Per task: records_retrieved (candidates), records_presented (selected in active, legacy_ids in shadow), memory_tokens, downstream_use = share of presented records whose files or components appear in the task's changed paths (gitutil.changed_paths when a worktree exists, else the result's files list) or whose id/title words appear in the result summary, first_pass (merged without a fix round: no task with constraints.fix_round_for equal to it), fix_rounds count, repeated_retrieval (same record presented to the same lineage more than once), irrelevant = presented and not used. Aggregate per mode and per 7 days: precision (used/presented), utility_per_token (used records / memory_tokens * 1000), first_pass rate for tasks with memory vs without. CLI `orchestrator scorecard --memory [--days n] [--json]`. Create orchestrator/memory_eval.py with the P34 memory cases as deterministic checks over a temp root seeded from fixtures: current decision found in HOT, older decision found in WARM by search, historical provenance (superseded decision) found in COLD by search with tier cold, an irrelevant record excluded from a task's tiered sections, compaction preserves knowledge (every record still findable after compact). run(root) -> {cases: [{name, passed, detail}], passed, total}; persist to .orchestrator/memory_eval.json like context_eval does; CLI `orchestrator memory-eval [--json]`. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/08-memory-scorecard.md.
Spec review T-1181 folded in: (1) kind is 'retrieval'. (2) downstream_use uses the paths the task actually changed: gitutil.changed_paths when the worktree still exists, else the file list of the task's commits on the goal branch (commits whose subject starts with the task id, read with git log --name-only on goal/<parent>), else task scope as the last fallback; document which source was used per task in the row. (3) memory_tokens is mode-conditional exactly like records_presented: tokens_tiered when the row's mode is active, tokens_legacy when shadow, so utility_per_token compares like with like; the report states the mode per aggregate.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.

risks.issue: The T-1181 fold-in fallback for downstream_use, when no worktree exists, calls for parsing `git log --name-only` on goal/<parent> and matching commits whose subject 'starts with the task id'. This duplicates and is strictly worse than data merge.merge() already writes: at merge.py:93-99, `changed_files = git("diff","--name-only", f"{previous_sha}..{sha}")` is computed from the exact merge commit range and stored directly on the bus task row via `bus.update(task_id, ..., changed_files=changed_files, ...)`. Every merged task already carries its precise changed-file list; no goal-branch history walk or commit-subject parsing is needed. Additionally, a raw `startswith(task_id)` prefix check is a real correctness bug independent of this: a commit subject 'T-1193 fix bug' also satisfies `startswith('T-119')`, so if a task T-119 exists its retrieval row would wrongly attribute T-1193's commits as its own changed paths.

suggested_spec_changes: Change the downstream_use fallback order to: gitutil.changed_paths when the worktree still exists -> task.get('changed_files') from the bus row (populated by merge.merge() at merge.py:98-99) when the task was merged -> task scope as the last fallback. Drop the git log --name-only / commit-subject-prefix parsing entirely; it is redundant with changed_files and, as specified, has a prefix-collision bug (task id 'T-119' would match commits for 'T-1193'). Keep the per-row 'source used' annotation the fold-in note already requires, now with values worktree|changed_files|scope.
